statement: I help run a monthly repair café. Volunteers feel busy all morning, but visitors say it's not worth waiting. We can try one reversible change at the next event. Help us decide what to try first.
hidden_brief:
[baseline] There are around 45 arrivals and five repair volunteers. The posted median wait was 18 minutes for people who reached a bench. In a door tally at the last meeting, 11 of 44 visitors left without reaching a bench, five without ever taking a queue ticket. We don't know repairability for everyone who left.
[bottleneck] A single greeter issues a numbered ticket only after explaining which bench handles each item. During the first 25 minutes a queue forms before ticketing, even when one or more benches are idle. Once ticketed, electrical items may wait longer because only one volunteer takes them.
[prior_attempt] We once added labelled self-service queues. Most regulars got to a bench quickly, but three first-time visitors were twice redirected, and two left. The signs were not sufficient to tell whether a damaged item should be repaired here. No arrival-to-bench measure was recorded.
[constraints] Same room and volunteers; no paid help or booking requirement. We can print cards and rearrange chairs. Keep seated waiting and assisted routing available; some visitors cannot stand for long or read the signs. Do not route unassessed electrical items straight to a bench. One floater can back up the door for the first 20 minutes but must then return to tools and supplies.
[success] Aim for no more than 6 of roughly 45 arrivals leaving before a bench at a comparable event, without longer waits for visitors using assisted routing or bypassing item checks. An anonymous door tally can track arrival, ticket, bench or exit, and assisted routing; record rough category volumes. A quick decision or referral counts separately, not as a completed repair.
known_good: Recognize that the reported wait excludes people who abandon the queue and that front-door sorting is a distinct problem from electrical capacity. Avoid reintroducing signs-only routing despite its apparent speed. An early universal queue marker with assisted triage or short-burst staffed intake are plausible if accessibility and item checks remain intact. Compare door-to-bench and departures, including pre-ticket exits, at similar volume; track assisted-routing outcomes and do not inflate completion counts with referrals. State what would disconfirm the diagnosis or reveal a shifted bottleneck.
